author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Every punishment is justice
english: Every punishment from Him is pure justice and every blessing from Him is pure grace.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Adhere to servitude
english: Whoever desires everlasting bliss, let him adhere firmly to the threshold of servitude.
reference: Reported by Ibn al-Qayyim, Madarij al-Salikin 1/153

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Guidance needs knowledge and patience
english: Guidance is not attained except with knowledge, and correct direction is not attained except with patience.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: A paradise in this world
english: In this world there is a paradise; whoever does not enter it will not enter the Paradise of the Hereafter.
reference: Reported by Ibn al-Qayyim, Al-Wabil al-Sayyib p. 69

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: The true prisoner
english: The one who is truly imprisoned is the one whose heart is imprisoned from Allah, and the captivated one is the one whose desires have enslaved him.
reference: Reported by Ibn al-Qayyim, Al-Wabil al-Sayyib p. 69

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Religion: truth, action, patience
english: The whole religion revolves around knowing the truth and acting by it, and action must be accompanied by patience.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Worship on the Law
english: Worship is founded upon the Legal Law and following it, not upon one's desires and innovation.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Taste the sweetness of deeds
english: If you do not taste the sweetness of an action in your heart, suspect it — for the Lord, Exalted is He, is the Appreciative.
reference: Reported by Ibn al-Qayyim, Madarij al-Salikin 2/68

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Love of the Master
english: The more the servant loves his Master, the less will he love other objects and they will decrease in number. The less the servant loves his Master, the more will he love other objects and they will increase in number.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Gratitude or repentance
english: The servant is perpetually either the recipient of a blessing from Allah — in which case he is in need of gratitude — or the perpetrator of a sin — in which case he is in need of repentance. He is always moving from one blessing to another and is always in need of repentance.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Sins and repentance
english: Sins cause harm and repentance removes the cause.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Tawhid opens; repentance closes
english: Bearing witness to Tawhid opens the door of good, and repentance from sins closes the door of evil.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Jihad against the soul
english: The jihad against the soul is the foundation for the jihad against the disbelievers and hypocrites.
reference: Reported by Ibn al-Qayyim, Rawdat al-Muhibbin p. 478

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Fear of other than Allah
english: A man will never fear something besides Allah unless it be due to a disease in his heart.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Trials like heat and cold
english: Trials and tribulation are like feeling the heat and cold: when one knows that they cannot be avoided, he will not feel anger at their onset, nor will he be distressed or disheartened.
reference: Reported by Ibn al-Qayyim, Madarij al-Salikin 3/289

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Delight of remembrance
english: In this world, man finds in the remembrance of Allah, praising Him and worshipping Him, a delight that is incomparable to anything else.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Objective of zuhd and worship
english: The objective of asceticism is to leave all that harms the servant's Hereafter, and the objective of worship is to do all that will benefit his Hereafter.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Sins as locks
english: Sins are like chains and locks preventing their perpetrator from roaming the vast garden of Tawhid and reaping the fruits of righteous actions.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: What can my enemies do
english: What can my enemies do to me? I have in my breast both my heaven and my garden. If I travel they are with me, never leaving me. Imprisonment for me is a chance to be alone with my Lord. To be killed is martyrdom, and to be exiled from my land is a spiritual journey.
reference: Reported by Ibn al-Qayyim, Al-Wabil al-Sayyib p. 69

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Follow only the Messenger
english: No one has to blindly follow any particular man in all that he enjoins or forbids or recommends, apart from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: People of Sunnah follow revelation
english: The people of truth and the Sunnah do not follow anyone unconditionally except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — who does not speak from desire; it is only revelation revealed to him.

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: The heart as a bird
english: The heart on its journey towards Allah the Exalted is like that of a bird. Love is its head, and fear and hope are its two wings. When the head is healthy, then the two wings will fly well. When the head is cut off, the bird will die. When either of the two wings is damaged, the bird becomes vulnerable to every hunter and predator.
arabic: القلب في سيره إلى الله عز وجل بمنزلة الطائر، فالمحبة رأسه، والخوف والرجاء جناحاه

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: The heart's emptiness
english: In the heart is a void that cannot be filled except by His love, turning to Him, always remembering Him, and being sincere to Him. Were a person to be given the entire world and everything in it, that would never fill the void.
arabic: وفيه فاقة لا يسدها إلا محبته والإنابة إليه ودوام ذكره وصدق الإخلاص له

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Loneliness of the heart
english: In the heart is a desolate feeling that cannot be removed except by intimacy with Him in solitude.
arabic: وفيه وحشة لا يزيلها إلا الأنس به في خلوته

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Anxiety of the heart
english: In the heart is anxiety that is not made tranquil except by gathering oneself for His sake and fleeing from everything to Him.
arabic: وفيه قلق لا يسكنه إلا الاجتماع عليه والفرار منه إليه

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Mercy over vengeance
english: Forgiveness is more beloved to Allah than vengeance, mercy is more beloved to Him than punishment, grace is more beloved to Him than justice, and giving is more beloved to Him than withholding.
arabic: والعفو أحب إليه من الانتقام، والرحمة أحب إليه من العقوبة

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Shari'ah is justice and mercy
english: The Shari'ah is founded upon wisdom and welfare for the servants in this life and the Hereafter. In its entirety it is justice, mercy, benefit, and wisdom. Every matter which abandons justice for tyranny, mercy for its opposite, benefit for corruption, and wisdom for foolishness is not part of the Shari'ah even if it was introduced therein by interpretation.
arabic: فإن الشريعة مبناها وأساسها على الحكم ومصالح العباد في المعاش والمعاد، وهي عدل كلها ورحمة كلها

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Faith: patience and gratitude
english: Faith consists of two halves: one half patience and the other half gratitude.
arabic: الإيمان نصفان: نصف صبر ونصف شكر

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Three signs of happiness
english: When blessed, the servant gives thanks; when tried, he is patient; and when sinful, he seeks forgiveness. These three are signs of a person's happiness and success in this world and the next.

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Supports of gratitude
english: Gratitude rests on three supports: recognizing the blessing inwardly, mentioning and thanking for it outwardly, and using it in a way that pleases the One who bestowed it.

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Heart's remedy
english: The heart becomes sick as the body becomes sick, and its remedy is repentance and refraining from sin. It becomes rusty as a mirror becomes rusty, and its polish is remembrance of Allah.

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Prefer Allah over desires
english: Whoever desires to purify his heart, let him prefer Allah to his desires. A heart clinging to its desires is veiled from Allah in proportion to its attachment to them.

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Imamate with patience and certainty
english: It is with patience and certainty that leadership in the religion is attained.
arabic: بالصبر واليقين تنال الإمامة في الدين
reference: Madarij al-Salikin (reporting Ibn Taymiyyah on Qur'an 32:24)

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Certainty completes knowledge
english: Certainty is the perfection of knowledge and its goal; by completing the rank of knowledge, leadership in the religion is obtained.

author: Imam Abu Hanifa
title: Stories of the scholars
english: The stories of the scholars and sitting with them are more beloved to me than much of fiqh — because they are the manners and character of the people.
arabic: الحكايات عن العلماء ومجالستهم أحب إلي من كثير من الفقه لأنها آداب القوم وأخلاقهم
reference: Ibn Abd al-Barr, Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm

author: Imam Abu Hanifa
title: Do not write every opinion
english: Woe to you, O Ya'qub! Do not write down everything you hear from me. I may hold an opinion today and leave it tomorrow, and hold an opinion tomorrow and leave it the day after.
arabic: ويحك يا يعقوب لا تكتب كل ما تسمع مني فإني قد أرى الرأي اليوم فأتركه غدا

author: Imam Abu Hanifa
title: Take the authentic hadith
english: If an authentic narration comes from the Prophet ﷺ, we take it and do not go beyond it.
arabic: إذا جاء الحديث الصحيح الإسناد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذنا به ولم نعده

author: Imam Malik
title: Knowledge is light
english: Knowledge is not abundant narration. Knowledge is only a light that Allah places in the hearts.
arabic: ليس العلم بكثرة الرواية إنما العلم نور يضعه الله في القلوب

author: Imam Malik
title: I am only human
english: I am only a human being. I err and I am correct. Look into my opinions: whatever agrees with the Book and the Sunnah, take it; whatever does not, leave it.
arabic: إنما أنا بشر أخطئ وأصيب فانظروا في رأيي فكل ما وافق الكتاب والسنة فخذوا به
reference: Ibn Abd al-Barr, Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm

author: Imam Malik
title: Argument extinguishes light
english: Disputation and argument about knowledge remove the light of knowledge from a man's heart.
arabic: المراء والجدال في العلم يذهب بنور العلم من قلب الرجل
reference: Ibn Rajab, Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam

author: Imam Malik
title: Everyone's statement can be left
english: Everyone's statement can be taken or left — except that of the occupant of this grave (the Prophet ﷺ).
arabic: كل أحد يؤخذ من قوله ويترك إلا صاحب هذا القبر
reference: Ibn Abd al-Barr, Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm

author: Imam Malik
title: Manners before knowledge
english: My mother would dress me and say: Go to Rabi'ah and learn from his manners before his knowledge.
arabic: كانت أمي تعممني وتقول لي اذهب إلى ربيعة فتعلم من أدبه قبل علمه

author: Imam al-Shafi'i
title: Leave my saying for the Sunnah
english: If you find in my book something contrary to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then speak according to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and leave what I said.
arabic: إذا وجدتم في كتابي خلاف سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقولوا بسنة رسول الله ودعوا ما قلت
reference: Al-Bayhaqi, Ma'rifat al-Sunan wa al-Athar; also Ibn Abi Hatim, Adab al-Shafi'i

author: Imam al-Shafi'i
title: Act on the authentic hadith
english: If a hadith is authentic and it contradicts my opinion, act upon the hadith and leave my opinion.
arabic: إذا صح الحديث خلاف قولي فاعملوا بالحديث واتركوا قولي

author: Imam al-Shafi'i
title: Argument hardens the heart
english: Arguing about the religion hardens the heart and breeds resentment.
arabic: المراء في الدين يقسي القلب ويورث الضغائن

author: Imam al-Shafi'i
title: Surat al-'Asr
english: If the people reflected upon this Surah (al-'Asr), it would suffice them.
arabic: لو تدبر الناس هذه السورة لوسعتهم

author: Imam al-Shafi'i
title: Debate with goodwill
english: I never debated anyone except with sincere goodwill.
arabic: ما ناظرت أحدا إلا على النصيحة

author: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
title: Take from where they took
english: Do not imitate me, nor Malik, nor al-Thawri, nor al-Awza'i — take from where they took.
arabic: لا تقلدني ولا تقلد مالكا ولا الثوري ولا الأوزاعي وخذ من حيث أخذوا
reference: Ibn Abd al-Barr, Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm

author: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
title: The proof is in the narrations
english: The opinion of al-Awza'i, the opinion of Malik, and the opinion of Sufyan — each is opinion, and it is all the same to me. The proof is only in the narrations.
arabic: رأي الأوزاعي ورأي مالك ورأي سفيان كله رأي وهو عندي سواء وإنما الحجة في الآثار
reference: Ibn Abd al-Barr, Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm

author: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
title: Good character is patience
english: Good character is that you do not become angry or fierce, and that you patiently endure what comes from people.
arabic: حسن الخلق أن لا تغضب ولا تحتد وحسن الخلق أن تحتمل ما يكون من الناس
reference: Ibn Rajab, Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam

author: Imam al-Bukhari
title: Prayer before writing
english: I did not write any hadith in the Sahih until I had performed ablution and prayed two rak'ahs.
reference: Al-Dhahabi, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' 12/402 (biography of al-Bukhari)

author: Imam al-Bukhari
title: Selected over many years
english: I compiled my Sahih over sixteen years, selecting authentic reports from among some six hundred thousand narrations.
reference: Al-Khatib, Tarikh Baghdad; Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari

author: Imam Muslim
title: Prefer the sound few
english: Turning to a small amount that is authentic is worthier than seeking abundance of what is weak.
arabic: فالقصد منه إلى الصحيح القليل أولى بهم من ازدياد السقيم

author: Imam Muslim
title: Transmit only the sound
english: It is obligatory upon everyone who can distinguish sound reports from weak ones, and trustworthy transmitters from those accused, that he transmit only what is known for the soundness of its path and the integrity of its narrators.

author: Imam al-Nawawi
title: Purpose of Riyad al-Salihin
english: I intended to compile a brief work of authentic narrations encompassing what a traveler on the path to the Hereafter needs — of manners for the limbs and hearts — arranging each chapter with verses of the Qur'an and then authentic hadith.

author: Imam al-Nawawi
title: On the Forty Hadith
english: These hadith comprise what concerns every Muslim in the affairs of his religion — outward and inward — so every person hoping for the Hereafter should know them.

author: Imam al-Nawawi
title: Intention of the student
english: The first duty of the seeker of knowledge is to purify his intention for Allah alone.

author: Imam al-Ghazali
title: Knowledge of the heart
english: Knowledge of the heart, its realities, and its qualities is the foundation of the religion and the basis of the path of the seekers. Whoever knows himself knows his Lord.
arabic: فمعرفة القلب وحقيقة أوصافه أصل الدين وأساس طريق السالكين

author: Imam al-Ghazali
title: Recite as a servant's letter
english: Do not make mere study of the Qur'an your task. Rather recite as a servant reads a letter from his Master that was written to him so that he may reflect upon it and act upon what it requires.
reference: Al-Ghazali, Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din — Adab Tilawat al-Qur'an

author: Imam al-Ghazali
title: Character is trained
english: These beautiful character traits can be acquired by training: at first one burdens oneself with the deeds that flow from them until they become one's nature at the end. This is among the wonders of the link between the heart and the limbs.
reference: Al-Ghazali, Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din — Kitab Riyadat al-Nafs

author: Imam al-Ghazali
title: Watch your heart and breaths
english: O seeker, you will not establish the commands of Allah until you watch over your heart and your limbs in your moments and your breaths.

author: Ibn Kathir
title: Tafsir method
english: The most correct method of tafsir is to explain the Qur'an by the Qur'an, then by the Sunnah, then by the sayings of the Companions, then by the Successors.

author: Ibn Kathir
title: Restrain rage and forgive
english: When rage rises in them, they restrain it — holding it back and not acting upon it — and with that they forgive those who wronged them.
arabic: إذا ثار بهم الغيظ كظموه بمعنى كتموه فلم يعملوه وعفوا مع ذلك عمن أساء إليهم

author: Ibn Kathir
title: Argue kindly
english: Whoever needs to debate them, let it be in the best manner — with gentleness, softness, and good speech.
arabic: من احتاج منهم إلى مناظرة وجدال فليكن بالوجه الحسن برفق ولين وحسن خطاب

author: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: Know Allah in ease
english: Know Allah in prosperity and He will know you in adversity.
arabic: تعرف إلى الله في الرخاء يعرفك في الشدة
reference: Ibn Rajab, Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam (hadith of Ibn 'Abbas)

author: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: The greater jihad
english: Courage is patience for a time. This is so in jihad against the outward enemy. Likewise is jihad against the inward enemy — the ego and desires — and that is among the greatest jihad.
arabic: الشجاعة صبر ساعة ... وكذلك جهاد العدو الباطن وهو جهاد النفس والهوى فإن جهادهما من أعظم الجهاد
reference: Ibn Rajab, Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam

author: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: Means then trust
english: A person takes wise means and strives through permissible causes, then relies upon Allah after his effort. Reliance does not contradict taking means; combining them may be better.
reference: Ibn Rajab, Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam

author: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: Soundness of the heart
english: The soundness of a servant's outward deeds, and his distance from the unlawful and doubtful, follows the soundness of his heart. If the heart is sound — empty of all but love of Allah and fear of what He hates — the deeds of the body become sound.
reference: Ibn Rajab, Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam (on the hadith of the heart)

author: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: Silence of the salaf
english: Those of the salaf who kept silent from much dispute did not do so from ignorance or inability, but from knowledge and fear of Allah.
arabic: فما سكت من سكت من كثرة الخصام والجدال من سلف الأمة جهلا ولا عجزا ولكن سكتوا عن علم وخشية لله

author: Al-Dhahabi
title: On speaking about men
english: May Allah have mercy on a man who knows his own worth and stops at his limit.
reference: Al-Dhahabi, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (method remarks on criticism of men)

author: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
title: On Bukhari's rank
english: The book of Bukhari is the most authentic book after the Book of Allah, by the agreement of the people of knowledge who speak with fairness.
reference: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari / Fath al-Bari — introduction

author: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
title: Perseverance in worship
english: That delight is not obtained by the worshipper except through patience upon hardship — for the seeker is exposed to obstacles and periods of laziness.

author: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
title: Determination in du'a
english: Determination in supplication means earnestness in it, and resolving that what is asked will occur (while relying upon Allah).
arabic: ومعنى الأمر بالعزم الجد فيه وأن يجزم بوقوع مطلوبه

author: Imam Abu Hanifa
title: Analogize from the Book
english: When a matter comes, look in the Book of Allah; if you do not find it, look in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; if you do not find it, look to the consensus of the Companions.
reference: Ibn Abd al-Barr, Al-Intiqa' fi Fada'il al-A'immah

author: Imam Abu Hanifa
title: Fear of Allah in fatwa
english: It is not lawful for anyone to take our saying unless he knows from where we took it.
reference: Ibn Abd al-Barr, Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm

author: Imam Abu Hanifa
title: This world is a farm
english: This world is the farm of the Hereafter.
reference: Attributed in classical adab collections; cited in later Hanafi biographical summaries

author: Imam Malik
title: This knowledge is din
english: This knowledge is religion, so look carefully from whom you take your religion.
reference: Muslim, Sahih — Introduction (cited from Ibn Sirin; Malik taught and applied this principle)

author: Imam Malik
title: The last of this ummah
english: The last of this ummah will not be set right except by that which set right its first.
reference: Cited by Ibn Taymiyyah, Majmu' al-Fatawa 1/374 (from Malik)

author: Imam Malik
title: Leave what you doubt
english: Leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not make you doubt.
reference: Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2518 (Malik narrates this prophetic principle extensively in Al-Muwatta)

author: Imam Malik
title: Action seals knowledge
english: Knowledge without action is like a tree without fruit.
reference: Ibn Abd al-Barr, Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm

author: Imam al-Shafi'i
title: Desire and blindness
english: If you fear Allah, He will suffice you against people; and if you fear people, they will not avail you against Allah.
reference: Ibn Abi Hatim, Adab al-Shafi'i wa Manaqibuhu

author: Imam al-Shafi'i
title: Companionship
english: Be with the people of hadith, for they are the most correct of people.

author: Imam al-Shafi'i
title: Anger and intellect
english: Anger is a live coal in the heart of the son of Adam.

author: Imam al-Shafi'i
title: Travel for knowledge
english: I never debated anyone wishing that he would err; rather I wished that Allah would make the truth flow on his tongue.

author: Imam al-Shafi'i
title: Enough for a man
english: Sufficient for a man as knowledge is that he fears Allah; and sufficient for him as ignorance is that he is amazed with his own knowledge.
reference: Ibn Abd al-Barr, Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm

author: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
title: The grave is the first stage
english: The grave is the first stage of the Hereafter; if one is saved from it, what comes after is easier, and if one is not saved from it, what comes after is harder.
reference: Ibn Rajab, Ahwal al-Qubur (citing Ahmad); also in classical Hanbali collections

author: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
title: People of hadith
english: If you see a man loving the people of hadith, then he is upon the Sunnah.

author: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
title: Silence is safety
english: I used to hear something and I would not speak until I had researched it for years.
reference: Abu Nu'aym, Hilyat al-Awliya (reports on Ahmad's caution)

author: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
title: Du'a of the oppressed
english: Beware the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and Allah.
reference: Principle Ahmad taught from Prophetic hadith (Bukhari 2448); emphasized in his counsel

author: Imam al-Bukhari
title: Making ablution for hadith
english: I did not write a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ except that I was in a state of purity.
reference: Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, Al-Jami' li Akhlaq al-Rawi

author: Imam al-Bukhari
title: Between me and the creation
english: I hope to meet Allah and that He will not take me to account for backbiting anyone.

author: Imam al-Bukhari
title: Knowledge is action
english: There is no good in a body that does not contain knowledge, and no good in knowledge that is not accompanied by action.
reference: Cited in classical biographical notices of Bukhari (Siyar tradition)

author: Imam Muslim
title: Selecting the authentic
english: I did not include in this book anything that they agreed upon as authentic.
reference: Muslim, Sahih — Introduction (statement of his methodology)

author: Imam Muslim
title: The chain is religion
english: The isnad is part of the religion; were it not for the isnad, whoever wished could say whatever he wished.
reference: Muslim, Sahih — Introduction (from Ibn al-Mubarak; foundational to Muslim's method)

author: Imam Muslim
title: Care before narration
english: I presented this Musnad of mine to Abu Zur'ah, and whatever he indicated as having a defect, I left.
reference: Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi / classical notices on Muslim's Sahih

author: Imam al-Nawawi
title: Intention before action
english: The actions of the limbs are not upright unless the actions of the hearts are upright.
reference: Al-Nawawi, commentary themes in Riyad al-Salihin / Al-Adhkar introductions

author: Imam al-Nawawi
title: Seeking knowledge
english: The seeker of knowledge should begin with purifying his intention for Allah alone.

author: Imam al-Nawawi
title: Gentleness
english: Know that the religion is ease, and that gentleness in all matters is beloved.
reference: Al-Nawawi, Riyad al-Salihin (chapter themes; prophetic counsel he compiled)

author: Imam al-Nawawi
title: Remember death
english: Remembering death frequently softens the heart and weans it from the world.
reference: Al-Nawawi, Riyad al-Salihin — Book of mourning / death chapters

author: Imam al-Ghazali
title: Knowledge that benefits
english: Knowledge without action is insanity, and action without knowledge is vanity.

author: Imam al-Ghazali
title: The heart's polish
english: The heart becomes rusty through sins, and it is polished by seeking forgiveness and remembrance.
reference: Al-Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din — Book of Tawbah / Dhikr themes

author: Imam al-Ghazali
title: Love of the world
english: Love of the world is the head of every sin.
reference: Al-Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din (citing earlier reports)

author: Imam al-Ghazali
title: Good character
english: Good character is the weightiest thing in the balance of the believer.
reference: Al-Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din — Book of Good Character (from Prophetic hadith he expounds)

author: Imam al-Ghazali
title: Sincerity
english: Sincerity is to take oneself out of creation by seeing the Creator alone.
reference: Al-Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din — Book of Intention and Sincerity

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: What is with Allah remains
english: Whatever is with Allah remains, and whatever is with other than Allah vanishes.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Trials purify
english: Trials and tribulations are a means of purification and elevation for the believer.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: The sound heart
english: The heart will not find rest except in the remembrance of Allah.

author: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Justice even with enemies
english: Allah supports a just state even if it is unbelieving, and does not support an unjust state even if it is believing.

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Sins darken
english: Sins leave traces upon the heart: darkness, weakness, constriction, and alienation from Allah.

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Gratitude and patience
english: Faith is of two halves: half is patience and half is gratitude.

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: The keys of good
english: If Allah wants good for a servant, He opens for him the door of humility and neediness.

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Time is life
english: A person's time is his life, and his life is his capital; wasting it is worse than wasting wealth.

author: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Love follows knowledge
english: The more the servant knows Allah, the more he loves Him.

author: Ibn Kathir
title: Best tafsir method
english: The best method of tafsir is to explain the Qur'an by the Qur'an, then by the Sunnah, then by the sayings of the Companions.

author: Ibn Kathir
title: Stories for lessons
english: Allah relates the stories of the prophets so that hearts may find assurance and take heed.
reference: Ibn Kathir, Tafsir (on narrative ayat; e.g. themes of Yusuf/Hud)

author: Ibn Kathir
title: Hold to the Jama'ah
english: Holding to the united body of the Muslims upon the truth is from the foundations of the religion.
reference: Ibn Kathir, Tafsir (on verses of unity / 3:103 themes)

author: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: Knowledge that softens
english: Beneficial knowledge is that which softens the heart and brings fear of Allah.
reference: Ibn Rajab, Jami' al-Ulum wa al-Hikam

author: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: Small deeds lasting
english: The most beloved deeds to Allah are those that are consistent, even if small.
reference: Ibn Rajab, Jami' al-Ulum wa al-Hikam (expounding Prophetic hadith)

author: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: This world a bridge
english: Be in this world as a stranger or a traveler.
reference: Ibn Rajab, Jami' al-Ulum wa al-Hikam (on the hadith of Ibn Umar)

author: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: Night prayer
english: The standing at night is the honor of the believer.

author: Al-Dhahabi
title: Criticism with fairness
english: May Allah have mercy on a man who knows his own measure.

author: Al-Dhahabi
title: Love of hadith
english: The love of hadith elevates a man, and abandoning it lowers him.

author: Al-Dhahabi
title: Fear your own self
english: I fear for myself more from my own self than from my enemy.

author: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
title: Opening Fath al-Bari
english: Praise be to Allah who made the chains of transmission a fortress for the Sunnah.
reference: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari / introduction themes to Fath al-Bari

author: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
title: Sincerity in authorship
english: I ask Allah that this work be purely for His Face.

author: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
title: Manners of the student
english: The student of hadith must combine precision with good manners toward his teachers.
reference: Ibn Hajar, Nukhbat al-Fikar / hadith sciences counsel

author: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
title: Hold to Bukhari and Muslim
english: The most authentic books after the Book of Allah are Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
